summary.headline: SYK and QCOM downgraded RED→AMBER on genuine 2-session rebounds (analysts calling the sell-offs overdone); EIX is the sole persisting RED, worsening further (-2.66%) with the Aug 31 wildfire-legislation deadline still the key date. COIN stabilizing, downgraded to AMBER. New AMBER: NTR (Jefferies downgrade + Q2 earnings tomorrow 8/5) and OKE (growth-deceleration downgrades matching its own key_risk). MARA resolved to GREEN on a clean rebound. CWAN roster-integrity bug persists a 36th consecutive day — PR #11 and #12 both still open/dirty; re-removed CWAN from portfolios.json on this run's branch again, but it needs Carson to merge one of the two PRs directly to actually land. AMD reports Q2 today after close — first hyperscaler-capex read of the season.

flags.headline: EIX down another 2.66% — wildfire-liability/credit-downgrade overhang continues to worsen ahead of the Aug 31 legislative deadline
flags.detail: EIX fell a further 2.66% to $71.46 (from $73.41), extending the post-earnings-call decline. No new tier-1 news found this run beyond what's already on file: CEO Pedro Pizarro's 7/30 warning that California IOUs face a 'strong likelihood' of credit-rating downgrades absent wildfire-liability-fund legislative action by the CA legislature's August 31 session close, and Barclays' downgrade to Equal Weight (PT $75 from $78). Q2 EPS itself beat ($1.54 vs $1.20 consensus) — this remains a liability/regulatory overhang, not an operating miss.
flags.thesis_link: Direct hit on EIX key_risk: 'Elevated debt-to-equity of 216% amplifies financial risk from future wildfire events, adverse rate case outcomes... a single catastrophic fire in SCE's territory could create material liability.' The credit-downgrade warning is that risk moving from hypothetical to a dated (8/31) legislative catalyst.

evidence.source: Utility Dive — Edison Q2 2026 earnings call recap

flags.headline: QCOM downgraded RED→AMBER: +2.62% on a sector-wide chip rebound, though the underlying Apple-modem risk is unchanged
flags.detail: QCOM rose 2.62% to $151.57, its second straight positive session, as chip stocks broadly rebounded and investors refocused on AI/data-center catalysts (targeting $40B non-handset revenue, $15B+ data-center revenue by FY2029). This is a price recovery, not a resolution of the underlying thesis risk — Qualcomm's own FQ3 commentary (Apple-related revenue down ~50% next quarter, next-iPhone modem share 'materially lower') stands. Downgrading from RED to AMBER to reflect that the acute post-earnings slide has stabilized; not resolving the flag.
flags.thesis_link: QCOM key_risk: 'Apple modem internalization — if Apple successfully develops in-house baseband modems, Qualcomm could lose its largest QCT customer (estimated 20-25% of chip revenue).' Risk itself unchanged; only the price reaction is improving.

flags.headline: SYK downgraded RED→AMBER: +4.79% second straight rebound session, analysts calling the post-earnings sell-off overdone
flags.detail: SYK rose 4.79% to $341.14, its second consecutive up session (+4.41% on 8/3 alone) following the post-Q2 growth-deceleration sell-off. Jefferies and William Blair both maintained Outperform ratings, citing that the core business remains strong and that the initial reaction was overdone. Downgrading from RED to AMBER given the two-session recovery; not fully resolved since the underlying premium-valuation-vs-organic-growth tension in the thesis is unchanged.
flags.thesis_link: SYK key_risk: 'Premium valuation at 22.4x forward earnings and PEG of 2.08 leaves minimal margin of safety — any organic growth miss against the 8-9.5% guidance could trigger multiple compression.' Price action suggests the market is un-pricing some of that compression for now.

flags.headline: COIN downgraded RED→AMBER: flat session (+0.14%), no new catalyst since the Q2 miss
flags.detail: Coinbase was essentially flat at $146.46 (+0.14%) — the post-Q2-miss slide has stopped moving, with no fresh negative (or positive) catalyst found this run. Still well off pre-earnings levels and the underlying thesis risk (crypto-trading-volume leverage) hasn't reversed, but downgrading from RED given the lack of continued deterioration.
flags.thesis_link: COIN key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in crypto trading volumes makes Coinbase a leveraged bet on crypto market sentiment' — materialized via the Q2 miss, now stabilizing rather than worsening.

flags.detail: See roster_integrity block above for full detail. Fix re-committed on this run's branch; underlying process gap (no merge step for Stock-Screener PRs) means it will not land without Carson merging PR #11 or #12 directly.

flags.detail: Fell a further 2.34% to $224.04 (from $229.40). No new tier-1 catalyst found this run beyond the already-known guidance digestion; extends rather than reverses the prior session's -6.39% move.

flags.headline: SUPV -1.47%, minor continued drift; Q2 earnings now 2 days out (8/6)
flags.detail: Down modestly to $9.37. No confirming tier-1 catalyst found this run. Earnings on 2026-08-06 is the next real data point and is now inside the near-term watch window.
flags.thesis_link: Consistent with SUPV key_risk: 'Argentine macroeconomic instability... could reverse reform progress and compress bank margins,' though no specific news confirms this as the driver — unconfirmed by tier-1 source.

flags.headline: AEM +1.53%, partial recovery from the gold-pullback drift
flags.detail: Up 1.53% to $147.54, a partial bounce from the prior session's -3.64%. Consistent with a broader gold-price stabilization; no company-specific development found. Not yet a full resolution.
flags.thesis_link: Touches AEM key_risk: 'Gold price reversion from current near-record levels... would significantly compress margins' — still a pullback/stabilization, not a reversion; held at AMBER.

flags.headline: NTR down 4.5% on a Jefferies downgrade, with Q2 earnings landing tomorrow (Aug 5)
flags.detail: Nutrien fell 4.5% in the 2026-08-03 session after Jefferies analyst Laurence Alexander cut the stock to Hold from Buy, slashing his price target to $63 from $96 on demand/supply risk beyond this year. Q2 2026 results are scheduled for 2026-08-05 (tomorrow), so some of the move may also be pre-earnings de-risking. Sourced via secondary aggregators (GuruFocus, QuiverQuant) reporting the Jefferies action, not a primary release — treating as AMBER rather than RED per the tier-1 evidence rule until a wire/primary source confirms the rating change and its rationale.

flags.headline: OKE down 2.8% today, extending a downgrade-driven slide on growth-deceleration concerns that matches a listed key_risk
flags.detail: ONEOK fell another 2.8% (to $88.23) amid continued pressure from Morgan Stanley (cut to Equalweight from Overweight, PT to $103 from $113) and Jefferies (cut to Hold from Buy) downgrades citing a less clear post-2026 growth path and rising capex needs. This directly matches OKE's own screener report key_risk. Exact dates of the downgrades are not pinned down precisely (secondary-aggregator sourcing only), so held at AMBER rather than RED pending tier-1 confirmation.
flags.thesis_link: Matches OKE key_risk: 'Growth deceleration — 2026 EPS guidance midpoint of $5.53 is only 2% above 2025's $5.42, with major growth projects not contributing meaningfully until 2027-2028' and 'Forward PEG of 2.18 implies growth expectations that current guidance doesn't support.'

flags.headline: MARA resolved to GREEN: +4.07% clean rebound, no negative catalyst ever confirmed
flags.detail: MARA rose 4.07% to $11.76, its second positive session, reversing the prior 'bearish drift' flag. No company-specific negative catalyst was ever confirmed for the earlier decline (consistent with broader crypto-miner volatility); resolving the flag.

flags.headline: CRDO +5.4% — today's biggest mover, on continued AI-infrastructure demand and bullish sell-side action
flags.detail: Credo Technology led the book's movers, up 5.4% to $218.32. No adverse news; move consistent with the broader AI-infrastructure connectivity cycle and recent bullish analyst action (BofA raised its price target to $340 from $252, Buy; Evercore ISI initiated at Outperform, $325 PT). Catalysts on track, thesis intact.
